'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Operation Southern Spear]]
**[[2026 United States strikes in Venezuela]]
***The death toll from the [[United States|U.S.]] [[airstrike]]s on [[Caracas]], [[Venezuela]], five days ago increases to 100 people, including 23 [[Bolivarian National Armed Forces of Venezuela|Venezuelan military]] personnel and 32 [[Cuban Revolutionary Armed Forces|Cuban personnel]]. [https://bnonews.com/index.php/2026/01/venezuela-says-death-toll-rises-to-100-after-u-s-operation-to-capture-maduro/ (BNO News)]
*[[SDF–Syrian transitional government clashes (2025–present)|SDF–Syrian transitional government clashes]]
**[[January 2026 Aleppo clashes]]
***As fighting between the [[Kurds in Syria|Kurdish]]-led [[Syrian Democratic Forces]] and the [[Syrian Army]] continues in [[Aleppo]], [[Government of Syria|Syrian authorities]] open an [[humanitarian corridor|evacuation corridor]] for tens of thousands of civilians to evacuate the city. [https://www.euronews.com/2026/01/08/syrian-authorities-urge-civilians-to-leave-aleppo-as-clashes-with-kurdish-forces-continue (Euronews)]
***The Syrian Army captures the [[Ashrafiyah, Aleppo|Ashrafieh]] neighbourhood of Aleppo after three days of fighting with the Syrian Democratic Forces. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/1/8/live-syrias-army-shells-sdf-positions-in-aleppo-neighbourhoods (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
**[[2025 Southern Yemen offensive]], [[Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war]]
***The [[Saudi Arabia]]-led coalition in [[Yemen]] claims that [[Southern Transitional Council]] (STC) president [[Aidarus al-Zoubaidi]] has fled to the [[United Arab Emirates]] through [[Somaliland]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1/8/saudi-led-coalition-says-stcs-al-zubaidi-fled-to-uae-via-somaliland (Al Jazeera)]

[https://www.trtworld.com/article/a299ec8a83e4 (AA via TRT World)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1/7/saudi-led-coalition-strikes-yemen-says-stc-leader-al-zubaidi-has-fled (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2025–2026 Iranian protests]]
**A [[Police Command of the Islamic Republic of Iran|police officer]] is reportedly killed during clashes with anti-[[government of Iran|government]] protesters in [[Malard]], [[Iran]], as the number of injured police officers rises to 568. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/police-officer-killed-in-protests-near-tehran-iranian-media/3793277 (AA)] [https://www.africanews.com/2026/01/08/iran-police-officer-killed-as-protests-over-cost-of-living-enter-12th-day/ (Africa News)]

**[[NetBlocks]] reports a [[2026 Internet blackout in Iran|total internet outage]] in [[Tehran]] and other Iranian cities, continuing the following day. Additionally, a statue of former [[Quds Force]] commander [[Qasem Soleimani]], who was killed in a [[Assassination of Qasem Soleimani|US airstrike in 2020]], is toppled. **The [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli military]] launches multiple attacks in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]], killing thirteen [[Palestinians]], including five children. [https://www.newarab.com/news/israeli-forces-kill-13-gaza-including-5-children (''The New Arab'')]

'''Business and economy'''

**The [[Cambodia]]n [[National Bank of Cambodia|central bank]] orders the [[liquidation]] of [[Prince Bank]] and suspends its operations after founder [[Chen Zhi (businessman)|Chen Zhi]] was indicted by the [[United States]] for [[Scam centers in Cambodia|large-scale fraud]] and extradited to [[China]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260108-cambodia-to-liquidate-bank-founded-by-accused-scam-boss (AFP via France 24)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Binaliw landslide]]
**At least one [[sanitation worker]] is killed when a [[landfill]] collapses in [[Cebu City]], [[Philippines]]. [[Search and rescue]] operations are ongoing for the 34 others reported missing, while 12 people are hospitalized. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/cebu-landfill-landslide-search-continues-for-survivors (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]
*A woman is killed in a [[shark attack]] off the coast of [[Saint Croix]] in the [[United States Virgin Islands]]. The species of the [[shark]] involved is currently unknown. [https://apnews.com/article/usvi-shark-attack-killed-american-virgin-islands-57ddb343ee8d4eccfebe237fa6d96f49 (AP)]

***Two people are hospitalized after being shot by [[United States Border Patrol|Border Patrol]] officers in [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]], [[Oregon]], [[United States]]. [https://www.kptv.com/2026/01/08/federal-agents-shoot-2-people-portland/ (KPTV-TV)]

**[[Laos]]' top leader, [[Thongloun Sisoulith]], is re-elected as the [[General Secretary of the Lao People's Revolutionary Party]], the most powerful position in the [[one-party state]]. *[[Catholic Church sexual abuse cases in Europe]]
**The [[Spanish Episcopal Conference]] and the [[Government of Spain|national government]] agree to let the [[Spanish Ombudsman|ombudsman]] determine [[Settlements and bankruptcies in Catholic sex abuse cases|compensation]] for victims of [[Catholic Church sexual abuse cases|clergy sexual abuse]] whose cases are time-barred or whose alleged abusers are deceased, opening a one-year [[Cause of action|claims process]] funded by the [[Catholic Church in Spain|Catholic Church]].
